before.summary: Textbook default output: a purple-to-blue glass card that stacks almost every AI tell and still never says what the feature does.

findings.rationale: This is the standard diagonal purple-blue-cyan gradient, and none of its colours come from the subject. It sets the generic tone of the whole card.

findings.evidence: "Our powerful AI-driven planning engine lets you seamlessly see the plan before any changes are made, empowering you to edit, reorder, or reject it with confidence."
findings.rationale: The sentence piles up buzzwords (powerful, AI-driven, seamlessly, empowering) and repeats the headline. The only specific claim is edit, reorder or reject the plan, and it is buried.

findings.evidence: White at alpha .08, .12, .18, .25, .28, .3, .35 and .7, plus opacity .72, .75 and .8 on text
findings.rationale: There are about a dozen one-off white alphas and no committed palette, so hierarchy turns to mud. Faded body text on the gradient also loses contrast.

findings.location: .slop h5 (line 18) and the Google Fonts link
findings.rationale: A tasteful default serif dropped onto a grotesk-and-mono product card that has no editorial or luxury context. Nothing else on the card uses it.
The italics land on arbitrary words for flavour, not for real stress.
A staccato campaign rhythm with no specific claim behind it. It could head any agent product.
A file path with arrows used as decoration on a marketing card. It is not shown as real product output.

findings.evidence: font: 500 11px var(--mono) on the eyebrow; 400 12px var(--mono) on the breadcrumb
findings.rationale: Monospace is worn as a technical costume on a label and a decorative path, not on real code.
A faded line of adjectives in small, tracked capitals that nobody reads and that carries no state.
The label PLAN repeats the heading and tells the reader nothing new.
A lone feature card has no real order, so the number only implies structure.
A filler badge that carries no state that changes.

findings.evidence: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.28/.3/.35); the pill and the buttons are bordered boxes inside the bordered .box
findings.rationale: Bordered boxes are nested inside a bordered box, where spacing would do the grouping.

findings.evidence: Two hairlines with border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.25) inside a short card
findings.rationale: Rules cut a five-line card into strips where whitespace would separate the parts.

findings.evidence: border-radius: 22px on the card, 12px on the buttons, 999px on the pill
findings.rationale: Soft radii are on every element, and there is no shared radius scale.

after.summary: A clean, committed card: specific headline, useful copy, one accent CTA, and the mono and file paths sit inside a real plan preview, so nothing here reads as a default.

findings.rationale: The paths are the example plan output the headline promises (see the plan before any file changes), not decoration. There are no arrows or comment syntax, and the '3 relevant' count is real data.

findings.evidence: font: 400 13px/1.6 var(--mono) — JetBrains Mono, with tabular-nums
findings.rationale: Monospace appears only in the plan preview, where it shows file paths a user would read as code. The heading, body and CTAs use Barlow and Big Shoulders.
There are two named mixes derived from a three-colour palette and no stack of alpha tints. The scan flagged them, but this is the token system the indicator recommends, not mud.

scan.verdict: Mostly intentional. Check those were choices

steps.note: Brief: A single feature card that presents one product feature. The page names no product, subject or audience, so a designer would first need to know what the feature belongs to and who it is for. Applied ground #1C2A30, light #E4E8E3, signal #FF6A1F; Big Shoulders Stencil Display with Barlow. 7 edits.

summary:
Score 15/20 before, 0/20 after.
Biggest moves: 15 fixes (Delete filler badges, Drop redundant labels, Unitalicize random words); a committed direction (#1C2A30/#E4E8E3/#FF6A1F, Big Shoulders Stencil Display); 1 polish edits.
Check by hand: The CTAs were already plain <span> elements with no href, so there were no links to preserve. They are still spans, now marked up as a primary button and a secondary link-style label; I rewrote the copy to 'Edit, reorder or reject the plan. Nothing runs until you approve it.' The second sentence restates 'see the plan before any changes are made' and adds no new claim, but please check the wording; open the result in a browser, confirm the signal colour sits on one element, and read the copy aloud.
